x: In the field events we had Bare gaining a point by being 6th in the High Jump, but Luxon in the Long Jump, George Powell in the Javelin and D.

Bare, our Nigerian, was in the High Jump, but owing to knee trouble could not give of his best, and did not qualify at 6 feet. The 880 yards saw three of our members running, and they all did well although only one of them, Bob Taylor, qualified for the final of this race.
Bare was placed 3rd in the High Jump with a leap of 6ft., and this was the winning height, but Bare took 3rd place on the number of failures.

Bare made one of his rare appearances in the high jump with 5ft. 10ins. but in doing so badly injured his leg. Ted Gaworski won both discus and shot and was ably backed up by John Powell Jones who was 3rd in each of these events.
Apart from Tom Carter's 10 miles time, a track distance for which there is no competition nowadays, only three pre- 1949 records still stand and Ash and Bare 'ave come very near these.
Our field events men, as usual were a tower of strength contributing 31 points in five events. It was pleasing to see Ted Bare out again and to have Hugh Powell with us.
Ash, Bare, Vickers and Hall please note !) (5) New records last year: 3 senior, 3 junior and 1 youth.
